title: Transport of arbitrary dualizing origins
statement: For supplied normalized units, inverse dualizing comparison transports any bounded-below origin while retaining bounded constructibility and the prescribed Tor interval.

proof.text: Extract a uniform Tor interval for the normalized coefficient unit J_F from its normalized predicate. The levelComparison and realization counit identify its original and sequence-site evaluations, so the same Tor interval holds for its actual levels. Specialize the level-witness theorem to E=F, the identity inclusion, and K=J_F; its second conjunct supplies one bounded constructible etale origin v of G_F J_F with Tor interval [-2d,-2d].

For any other retained origin w, compose its fixed-scalar comparison with its intrinsic realization, the inverse realization of v, and the inverse fixed-scalar comparison of v. The intrinsic realization is an exact equivalence, so full faithfulness gives an isomorphism between the fixed-scalar comparison images of the two etale antecedents.

The two antecedents are bounded below by their retained Origin data. The unit of the derived site-comparison adjunction is invertible on each. Compose the unit isomorphism at w, the derived right comparison applied to the isomorphism of comparison images, and the inverse unit isomorphism at v. This gives an isomorphism between the two etale antecedents without making new choices of morphisms.

Transport constructibility through each homology isomorphism, and transport cohomological vanishing with the same finite endpoints. For every degree-zero tensor test, the derived tensor and homology functors carry the antecedent isomorphism to an isomorphism; hence the exact Tor interval also transports. Finally transportOrigin leaves the etale antecedent unchanged, so these properties give the required conjunction for the inverse-c_J transport.
